stem: Which endoscopic finding is characteristically described as 'crepe paper mucosa' in patients with Eosinophilic Esophagitis (EoE)?

options.text: Fragility and tearing of the esophageal lining.
Cobblestoning of the lower esophageal sphincter.
Circular esophageal rings and focal strictures.

explanation: Crepe paper mucosa refers to the mucosal fragility and edema that can occur in the esophagus of EoE patients.
rationale: Focus on the physical texture and integrity of the esophageal lining described in the source.

optionExplanations.A: Crepe paper mucosa refers to the mucosal fragility and edema that can occur in the esophagus of EoE patients.
optionExplanations.B: Cobblestone appearances are more typical of other inflammatory bowel conditions rather than the specific esophageal changes in EoE.
optionExplanations.C: While these are common findings in EoE, they are distinct from the specific 'crepe paper' description of the mucosa.
optionExplanations.D: EoE typically presents with white exudates or pale patches rather than yellowish pseudomembranes.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: Fragility and tearing of the esophageal lining.
